lessons: Never repeat the video title or headline in the opening line; repeating the prompt (e.g., Potato Sprout video) caused immediate viewer drops of up to 31.9%.

Anchor hooks in concrete, extreme comparisons or mind-boggling statements (e.g., 'older than the United States', tuna vs. cod color contrast) which consistently yield high 10% retention (>1.2) and end retention (>0.85 vs. similar).
Avoid artificial delays like 'Pause and guess' or countdowns; these moments trigger immediate drop-offs at mid-video (e.g., Maple Syrup at 52% and Foil at 37%).
Skip stating the obvious physical setup or relatable feeling (e.g., 'You feel that pins-and-needles sensation') and jump directly into the unexpected counter-intuitive scientific cause.
Sustain retention toward the end by introducing deeper scale or secondary mysteries (e.g., Greenland Shark cold metabolism, Webb infrared heat glow) rather than relying on rapid loops.
worst_moment_types: Verbatim repetition of the video title/question in the first 10 seconds
Interactive pauses and countdown prompts ('Pause and guess...')
Slow, obvious setup lines describing relatable everyday sensations before giving new information
best_hook_types: Extreme chronological or historical anchor facts ('older than the United States')
Direct sensory/visual paradoxes ('slice a tuna steak... deep red beef, while a cod fillet is bright white')
Challenging established foundational knowledge ('Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge, yet...')
